summary: The saved game lost aliased floor objects and the lit lantern timer/light chain. The snapshot now preserves shared object identity, serializes global timers and light sources, and reconnects them before gameplay. The selected two-segment recording matches all 202 steps.

source.branch: save.c:savegamestate saves global timers and lights before inventory; save.c:savelev_core writes the floor chain through saveobjchn. restore.c:restgamestate restores global timers/lights and getlev/restobjchn rebuild floor objects. JS snapshots now preserve identity links and save timer_base/light_base; restore reconnects the graph before reinstating those roots.
callers: C save.c:dosave0 calls savelev and savegamestate; JS save.js:dosave0 calls serializeGameState.
C restore.c:dorecover calls restgamestate and getlev; JS jsmain.js restore entry calls restore.js:dorestore, which restores the snapshot and level objects.
source.javascriptOwner: js/save.js:serializeSnapshot previously replaced every repeated object with null and dosave0 omitted global timer/light roots. js/restore.js:dorestore previously parsed ordinary JSON with those aliases permanently lost; it now reconnects saved paths and restores the timer/light chains before inventory.
source.fix: Preserve shared object identity in JSON using first-path references and reconnect those references after parsing. Serialize global timer_base/light_base roots and restore them before inventory, matching restgamestate ordering.

evidence: The admitted v55 manifest firstMismatch identifies segment 1 step 0: C row 7 column 57 contains gold while JS contains floor; the source trace counts 30 floor objects before save and 14 after restoration, with gold o_id 23 absent.
save.c:savelev_core calls saveobjchn for fobj at lines 545-547; restore.c:getlev calls restobjchn for fobj at line 1166 then find_lev_obj().
restore.c:restobjchn constructs one object per saved chain record and links the nobj chain; saveobjchn writes each floor object and recursively writes container contents.

save.c:savegamestate calls save_timers(RANGE_GLOBAL) and save_light_sources(RANGE_GLOBAL) before saveobjchn for inventory; restore.c:restgamestate calls restore_timers(RANGE_GLOBAL) and restore_light_sources() before restoring inventory.

JS save.js:safeStringify uses a WeakSet and writes null for every repeated reference, not only cycles on the active traversal stack; restore.js:rebuildObjectList can only recover objects still present in level.objects.

JS save.js:dosave0 serializes the state snapshot without gt.timer_base or gl.light_base; restore.js:dorestore consequently has no saved global burn timer for the carried lantern, matching the later end_burn error.

At the current claimed base, the selected recording reaches segment 1 and stops at end_burn: lit object has no burn timer. The immutable accepted evaluation supplies the earlier mismatch and cell-level comparison; no new C recording was made.

The accepted baseline identifies segment 1 step 0 as the first mismatch: C shows gold at row 7 column 57 and JS shows floor. Its captured comparison reports 30 floor objects before save and 14 after JS restore, missing gold o_id 23/type 438/quantity 5.

C save.c:savegamestate calls save_timers(RANGE_GLOBAL), save_light_sources(RANGE_GLOBAL), then saveobjchn for inventory; restore.c:restgamestate restores global timers and lights before restobjchn. JS now preserves the shared object references and timer/light roots across the same boundary.

A bounded replay at the task base confirmed the later end_burn: lit object has no burn timer error, consistent with the baseline; the exact post-fix replay removes the error and matches both segments.

after.command: node scripts/run-bounded.mjs focused -- node scripts/scan-sessions.mjs --json --synthetic v55/v55-lantern-save-restore-action2
after.result: All 202 recorded screens, cursors, RNG calls and input boundaries matched across both segments; the replay had no command refusal, runtime error or unported behavior.
